correctness.rationale: All labeled single n-cycles biject with phases a1=0 and a2,...,an distinct in Z/n. Replacing the time-0 row bit gives exact prefix-indicator shift equations. The shifts realizing any prefix form a coset of a stabilizer of order dividing both n and the prefix cardinality; multiplication gives U(n). For prime powers, digit reversal makes each i-prefix stable under the largest subgroup of order p^{v_p(i)}. Independent suffix shifts by those subgroups preserve the complete comparison matrix and all future maximal prefix stabilizers; counting distinct shifts gives p^{(p^k-1)/(p-1)-k}. If n has distinct prime divisors p<q, equality forces nested prefixes S_p and S_q to equal incomparable subgroups of orders p and q, contradiction. Actual packaged Python checker passed prime powers 4,8,9,16,25 and exhaustive phase/iterate enumeration n4,6,8,9. Computation is not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 interval-map paper establishes a genuine sharp prime/composite identifiability distinction but supplies only existence of composite ambiguity. The theorem discovers and proves the exact maximal ambiguity for an infinite, natural arithmetic family of periods, together with a structural obstruction for all other periods. The count can be exponentially large and is directly informative about inverse reconstruction from dynamical order comparisons; it is not a textbook renaming, arbitrary finite slice or a routine improved implementation. General mixed-prime maxima remain open.
